editorial:
Imagine feeling like the world is judging you no matter what size you are. You follow Jamie, a young guy struggling with both anorexia and bulimia. He spent years getting teased for being overweight, so he pushed himself to lose weight fast. Now, he is stuck in a weird spot where people praise his new look, but he feels more alone than ever. The vibe is very quiet and personal, making you feel like you are stepping right into his head to see how he views the people around him.

What really works here is how the movie focuses on the 'why' instead of just the 'how.' You get to see Jamie realize that his new life is kind of a lie. The acting is solid and keeps things grounded, though the slow pace might feel a bit heavy for some. If you want a deep character study, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jamie stops trying to hide his pain from everyone. He finally admits that his obsession with weight was just a way to feel in control. He does not magically get cured in one second, but he reaches a point of honesty. The movie ends with him accepting that he needs help and realizing that the image he created for others was not real, leaving you with a hopeful feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about mental health and personal growth.
